- When sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., recent +1.00 or +0.67) and news volume is high, model tends to overreact — cap forecast peak at 10–15% below true outcome if recent sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment turns negative sharply (e.g., -1.00 or -0.67) within last 3–5 days, model often undercorrects — adjust forecast downward by 5–10% of recent range to avoid lagged bearish bias.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +/–0.33 or 1.00) — apply smoothing filter: average last 5 days’ true values before projecting next 30d.
- If sentiment change is +0.67 or higher and news volume is low, model tends to over-forecast — reduce forecast by 3–5% to account for sentiment lag.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00 or 0.33) and news volume is high, model often overestimates — apply downward bias of 2–4% to avoid “noise-driven” spikes.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% in 3–5 consecutive days, apply “mean reversion” correction: subtract 1–2% per day until forecast aligns with recent 7-day average.
- For sentiment +1.00 with low news volume, model often underestimates — add 2–4% to forecast to capture hidden bullish momentum.
- If sentiment change is +0.33 and news volume is high, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 10% below true outcome if sentiment is trending up.
